transcript:
Header: 2026-07-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Miriam, Lena, Ben, Dev, Asha, Tom, Priya, Kyle

Summary: quick sync before limited launch next week; go through perf issues, incident notes from last week, and signoffs.

[00:00] Miriam: okay, uh thanks everyone for joining, i think we have a tight agenda so let's try to keep to the points, first item is the p95 latency regression that showed up after the attention kernel change last week. Lena, can you give a quick status?

[00:28] Lena: yeah, sure. so we rolled the new attention kernel to staging, we saw a 8 to 12ms p95 bump on longer contexts, it's consistent with what we saw in canary but the canary sample size was small so it didn't trip our alert, um, we added more instrumentation yesterday and i have two hypotheses, one is the memory access pattern on A100 with the new tiling, and two is a threading mismatch with our runtime scheduler.

[01:05] Ben: to add, the spike on 7-21, the incident we looked at, seems correlated with concurrent compactions on the KV cache plus the kernel change. the compaction job overlapped canary traffic window which caused a small increase in latency and a few timeouts.

[01:30] Dev: yeah i reproduced locally with a simulated compaction cycle and high qps and saw the jitter. i think we need a quick fix to stagger compactions and a tighter lock around the KV cache page table.

[02:00] Miriam: okay so immediate mitigation is stagger compactions and revert threading tweak if needed. Lena, what's the plan for the kernel? full revert or hotfix?

[02:18] Lena: i want to try a hotfix first; it's smaller risk and should address memory access pattern—if perf doesn't improve we'll revert. i'll run three perf suites overnight and post numbers.

[02:40] Asha: quick Q on QA coverage, do we have regression tests that simulate compaction during high throughput? last run i looked at didn't exercise that path well.

[02:55] Dev: we had a test but it was low fidelity; i'll work with Asha to increase concurrency and add a chaos test for compaction overlap.

[03:12] Priya: from product-ops side, timeline matters: customers in the pilot cohort expect limited launch 2026-08-04, if we slip we should notify them by EOD Friday.

[03:30] Kyle: also canary thresholds need to be tuned—current rules are p95 + 10% and error rate + 3%, but given model variance we should consider a dynamic baseline for p95.

[03:50] Ben: i propose we change canary automation to evaluate relative to a rolling baseline and add a hard p95 delta of 20ms and a 5% error tolerance as a safety stop for this release.

[04:12] Miriam: sounds reasonable. Ben, can you own that and have it in place by Monday?

[04:20] Ben: yep, i'll have the automation update and unit tests in place by 2026-07-30.

[04:30] Miriam: on the incident review from 2026-07-21, let's talk mitigation and long-term fixes. Ben, do we have root cause in the doc?

[04:42] Ben: root cause is KV cache compaction colliding with canary traffic plus a regression in the attention kernel's memory layout. immediate mitigation was to pause scheduled compactions during canary windows, hotfix for kernel is in flight. long-term we'll add compaction backoff and make compaction preemptible.

[05:10] Lena: small note—some of the telemetry keys are mis-labeled in staging, e.g., attention_kern_v -> attn_kern_v, so dashboards didn't show the new metric. that made triage slower.

[05:28] Miriam: oof ok we need a checklist to validate metric names after deploy, Priya can you add that to the rollout checklist?

[05:36] Priya: yes, i'll add telemetry verification steps and owner.

[05:44] Asha: testing plan: i'll run full regression across seq lengths [64,256,1024], and stress with compaction overlap sims; ETA Monday morning for results.

[06:00] Dev: i'll instrument logs to capture compaction timestamps and add a flag to make compaction window configurable per cluster.

[06:20] Miriam: docs/runbooks—who's updating the incident playbook? we should include recovery steps if canary trips in production.

[06:30] Kyle: i can update the runbook and include rollback commands, how to disable compactions, and an emergency revert play. will do by 2026-08-02.

[06:45] Lena: one more technical point—there's a small inconsistency in kernel builds between our buildfarm nodes and the main CI image; i tracked to a different gcc minor version which changes codegen. i'm aligning toolchain and will recompile the kernel artifacts.

[07:10] Dev: thanks, that might explain some of the weird perf diffs.

[07:20] Miriam: okay, let's capture concrete acceptance criteria for canary: 1) p95 regression <= 10ms relative to baseline OR within rolling baseline delta, 2) error rate change <= 3% relative, 3) no more than 0.5% of requests time out, 4) no compaction-triggered anomalies in logs. Ben to implement automation.

[08:05] Ben: noted. i'll also add a suppression window for scheduled background jobs during canary.

[08:20] Asha: QA will gate on test matrix passing and will not sign off unless compaction sim passes.

[08:32] Miriam: good. last item: communications. Priya, prepare a short note to pilot customers with possible limited degradation and contingency plan; also share canary schedule.

[08:45] Priya: will do, target to send by Friday EOD.

[09:00] Miriam: recap next steps: lena runs hotfix + perf, ben updates canary automation, asha finishes regression matrix, dev increases compaction tests, kyle updates runbook, priya drafts customer comms. we'll meet on Monday for status and final go/no-go slot on 2026-08-03 16:00 UTC. any blockers?

[09:28] Lena: none from me, just need CI cycles.

[09:35] Ben: need permission for extra canary infra for wider sample, Miriam can approve?

[09:45] Miriam: yes, you have approval to spin up temporary canary nodes within quota.

[09:55] Tom: minor note, some internal stakeholders asked for a short debrief doc after go/no-go—can we capture that?

[10:05] Miriam: yes, i'll write a 1-pager and share.

[10:20] (crosstalk) Kyle: okay thanks everyone, we'll sync Monday.

End of transcript.
